result:
I renamed the XSRF cookie to `_mitmproxy_xsrf` on both the server and the frontend. I haven't run any tests or built anything.

- **Where it's set:** `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` now passes `xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf"` to the Tornado application. This changes the name of the cookie Tornado sets. It also changes the name Tornado reads back when it validates the token.
- **Where it's read:** `web/src/js/utils.ts` now reads `_mitmproxy_xsrf` instead of `_xsrf` when it builds the `X-XSRFToken` header.
- **Changelog:** I added an entry to `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Not verified:** Tornado isn't installed here, so I couldn't confirm that the `xsrf_cookie_name` setting exists. I'm relying on memory that it does. Please check it against the version pinned in `pyproject.toml`.

**Not done:**
- The prebuilt bundle `mitmproxy/tools/web/static/index-*.js` still reads the old cookie name. It needs a frontend rebuild, which I didn't do.
- I didn't add or change any tests. The existing ones only cover the case where XSRF checking is turned off, and `utilsSpec.tsx` only expects an undefined `X-XSRFToken`.
